issues.detail: Skill covers common error scenarios but lacks guidance for malformed API responses, rate limiting failures, and handling missing CSV fields.
Curl and bash examples assume Unix-like environment; Windows users without WSL would need PowerShell equivalents.

scenarios.name: sentry-critical-triage
scenarios.rationale: Response B explicitly commits to P1/P2/P3 prioritization, trend analysis (increasing/stable/decreasing), duplicate detection, and severity keyword flagging—all core rubric items—while Response A omits the P1/P2/P3 system, trend tracking, and duplicate merging; neither explicitly mentions root-cause grouping by file/line/function, but Response B's structured output plan better matches the rubric's requirements.

scenarios.name: csv-duplicate-detection
scenarios.rationale: Response B explicitly names and commits to all three rubric requirements (normalize with specific examples of variable types to strip, cluster by stack trace + normalized message, produce consolidation report with specific merge groups). Response A vaguely promises clustering and summary but doesn't clearly articulate the normalization strategy, stack trace origin approach, or specific merge recommendations required by the rubric.

scenarios.name: self-healing-vs-persistent
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly addresses all rubric elements (occurrence gaps >7d, resolved-but-recurring patterns, trend direction, user reach, ranking criteria) with specific operational thresholds and actionable deprioritization cutoffs; Response A mentions gaps and recurrence vaguely but omits trend analysis and user-reach metrics, offering only generic promises without the detailed ranking framework the rubric requires.
